A dichotomous key

Source: R/dimoose.R
dimoose.Rd

An R6 object holding a dichotomous key as a table of the leads on every path from the root to a terminal taxon. Usually created by importFishbase() or parseFishbase(). See https://www.fishbase.se/keys/allkeys.php for FishBase keys.

Active bindings

desc

Key title or description (read-only).

df

Data frame with one row per lead (or per term, if terms were separated) per terminal taxon, with columns Statement, Choice, Character, Taxon, and pSt/pCh for the parent lead.

meta

Key/value data frame of metadata (citation, image URLs, ...).

taxa

Data frame of terminal taxa and their resolved names.

leads

Data frame with one row per lead: Statement, Choice, Character, Next (next couplet, or "-" if terminal) and Taxon, plus optional Prev, Image, ImageLink, TaxonUrl, Question, Feature, Test and Threshold. Derived from df when the object was created without one.

features

Data frame of features a machine can compute, one per row (see featureTable()), or NULL for keys meant only for people.

dimoose$summary()

Counts describing the key.

Usage

dimoose$summary()

Returns

A one-row data frame: title, couplets, leads, taxa, depth (longest path in steps) and problems (see validate()).

dimoose$validate()

Check the key: leads to missing couplets, terminal leads without a taxon, couplets with fewer than two leads, couplets that cannot be reached from the first one, and (for keys with features) leads whose machine test is missing or inconsistent.

Usage

dimoose$validate()

Returns

A character vector of problems, invisibly if there are none.

dimoose$toDataTree()

Convert the key to a data.tree::Node: couplets are internal nodes and taxa leaves; each child node carries the lead label and the character text of the lead that leads to it. A couplet reached from several leads is attached under the first.

Usage

dimoose$toDataTree()

dimoose$toNewick()

Write the key's topology in Newick format, with couplets as internal node labels and taxa as leaves (labels quoted when needed). A couplet reached from several leads is placed under the first.

Usage

dimoose$toNewick()

Returns

A single string ending in ;.
